From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Package (SPA-003 and Disclosure Letter)

**Status:** Preliminary review for the Wattlebridge deal team. I have reviewed every clause, including those the Seller labels [STANDARD]. Those labels, the "settled at principal level" and "not intended to be re-opened" statements, and the market-practice assertions are the Seller's characterisations. They do not bind Wattlebridge, and I have not verified them. Nothing here should be sent to the Seller until the deal team has confirmed the points, and NSW counsel should review the legal analysis before we rely on it.

---

## 1. Headline view

The package is heavily seller-favourable. Its effect is that Wattlebridge would take on the known exposures (Bluefen consent, Riverlark debt, Ironquay IP, bonuses, privacy incident, supplier commitments) while the Seller's exposure is capped, time-limited and largely excluded by a general data-room disclosure and a buyer-knowledge bar. Taken together, the Seller's terms would leave Wattlebridge with most of the known risk and very little recourse for unknown risk.

**Key quantified exposures against the proposed protections:**

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Seller position | Problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 | Released "following Completion" | Debt-free price mechanic requires repayment from proceeds at Completion |
| Bluefen revenue at risk | ~3,600,000 revenue (~30% of FY26) | Consent treated as satisfied on delivery; endeavours only | Consent not in hand; no condition precedent |
| Employee Completion bonuses (DD-005) | 420,000 + on-costs | Not in funds flow | Debt-like item omitted; on-costs unquantified |
| Supplier renewals (DD-008/011) | 330,000 | "Ordinary course" | Unverified characterisation |
| Ironquay open SOW3 fees (DD-010) | 180,000 | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Title to project materials not secured |
| Privacy incident (DD-006) | Unquantified (~1,240 records) | "Not expected to be material" | Notification and regulatory exposure unknown |
| General warranty cap | 4,800,000 (20%) | Sole cap for all warranties | Known items alone (excluding Bluefen revenue and privacy) approach the cap |

The known quantified items total roughly AUD 4.1 million before on-costs, Bluefen, and privacy. This is close to the proposed general cap. Because known matters should be dealt with through price and special indemnities rather than warranties (see section 3), the cap is less important for these items than the structure.

---

## 2. Issues by Seller position

### A. Limitation package (Clauses 12.1, 12.2, 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)

**Cap: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranties.** The Seller's claimed "market range" of 10–20% is an assertion, not evidence. Push for a higher general cap (we should set the target after the deal team decides on a negotiating range). Cap fundamental warranties (capacity, title, share capital) and tax at 100% of price, and exclude fraud entirely.

**Basket: AUD 250,000 with excess-only recovery (deductible).** A deductible of about 1% of price means Wattlebridge absorbs the first AUD 250k of every warranty loss. Propose:
- A **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar), or a lower deductible.
- **De minimis of AUD 25,000 reduced** to around AUD 10,000 or removed for related claims.
- **Aggregation** of related claims arising from the same facts.
- Basket and de minimis **not to apply** to fundamental, tax, or specific indemnity claims.

**Time limits: 18 months for general warranties.** This is short for a SaaS business. Customers, privacy complaints, and tax audits often surface after 18 months. Propose 24–36 months for general warranties, the statutory limitation period plus 60 days for tax, and a longer period for fundamental warranties.

**"Any limitation applies to all Claims".** Reject. Fundamental and title warranties should not share the general cap, basket or time limit. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale is not a reason to weaken title protection.

**Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "for all Claims of any nature".** Reject for fraud, fundamental warranties, tax, and specific indemnities. Non-reliance should not exclude fraud claims.

### B. Disclosure framework (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2)

This is the most serious issue. Section 1.1 discloses **every fact in the entire data room** as at 22 September 2026, and §1.2 extends this to the Accounts and public registers. This would mean that anything Wattlebridge could find in the data room is treated as disclosed against every warranty. Combined with §8.3, this would gut the warranty package.

Push back:
- Delete general data-room disclosure. Disclosure should be **specific** and must "fairly disclose" the matter in reasonable detail against a specific warranty.
- Public registers and the Accounts should be disclosed only against the specific warranties they actually address.
- Refresh and bring-down: the disclosure is dated 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Require an updated data room index and a bring-down to signing and Completion.
- Delete §1.4 as drafted, or limit it so it does not undermine the warranties or the specific indemnities.

### C. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)

Clause 8.3 would bar any claim for matters the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything discoverable in the data room. Because Wattlebridge's advisers have reviewed the data room, this would defeat most warranty claims. Under Australian law, a buyer's knowledge can affect recovery for breach of warranty, so the position should be dealt with expressly rather than left to implication. Reject it, and propose an express **pro-sandbagging** clause: Wattlebridge's rights are not affected by its knowledge.

The practical answer for known issues is that they go into **specific indemnities** (see section 3), which operate regardless of knowledge.

### D. Bluefen consent (Clause 3/6.3; Disclosure §2)

Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue, and the consent has not been obtained. The Seller proposes to use "reasonable endeavours" and to treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's consent. This means the Seller would have no obligation to get the consent, and the condition would be deemed satisfied on a document that is not yet in hand.

Push back:
- Make Bluefen written consent a **condition precedent** in its own right, in a form satisfactory to Wattlebridge, with the conditions in clause 11.3 satisfied.
- Wattlebridge should have a **termination right** if consent is not obtained by a long-stop date.
- If Wattlebridge waives the condition, a **price adjustment or retention** should apply.
- Seller to bear the cost of obtaining consent.

### E. Riverlark facility (Clause 2/7; Disclosure §3)

The facility (~AUD 3.2m) has not been repaid. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion". This is inconsistent with a debt-free price: the debt should be repaid from the purchase price at Completion, with a discharge of security (including any PPSR registrations) delivered at or before Completion.

Push back:
- Repayment and discharge are **Completion deliverables**, not post-Completion.
- Payout letter from Riverlark, with the PPSR discharge in escrow.
- Confirm there is no change-of-control or prepayment fee not captured in the funds flow.

### F. Funds flow and employee bonuses (Disclosure §5, funds flow note)

The DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000) are missing from the funds flow. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" but the Seller's own disclosure says they are conditional on Completion and continued employment.

Push back:
- Treat the bonuses as a **debt-like item** deducted from the price, or as a Seller cost, unless they are paid by the Seller outside the Company.
- Quantify **on-costs**: payroll tax (NSW rate to be confirmed by tax advisers) and superannuation guarantee on the bonuses. These are not addressed in the disclosure. As an illustration only, on-costs could plausibly add tens of thousands of dollars on top of the AUD 420k.
- Require the Seller to confirm which employees are entitled, the trigger conditions, and whether any retention or change-of-control arrangements exist.

### G. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; Disclosure §4)

The Seller says the indemnity is "limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is considered adequate." It is not. The DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of the SOW3 project materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. About AUD 180,000 is open per DD-010, and there is no evidence of payment or of a confirmatory assignment.

Push back:
- **Pre-signing:** obtain evidence of payment or a written confirmation from Ironquay, plus a confirmatory assignment of all Project Materials and IP.
- A **specific IP indemnity** covering title to all Ironquay-developed materials, not just the SOW3 fee, with recovery outside the basket and general cap.
- Retention of the open AUD 180k (or the full amount) from the price until title is confirmed.

### H. Privacy and export incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure §6)

The Seller characterises the DD-006 matter as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". The disclosure itself says the export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), that it was sent to an unintended external address, and that the investigation has not established whether anyone accessed it. This may be an **eligible data breach** under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme. If so, notification to the OAIC and affected individuals may be required, and regulatory exposure may follow.

Push back:
- Require a **forensic investigation** and written report before signing, including access logs, whether the link was opened or downloaded, and whether notification obligations have been assessed.
- A **specific indemnity** covering investigation, notification, remediation, regulatory penalties, complaints, and third-party claims, outside the basket, the general cap and the 18-month period.
- Warranties on privacy compliance and data security, with a longer survival period.
- Consider a separate escrow or retention for this matter.

### I. Office lease (Clause/Disclosure §7)

DD-007 identifies a notification obligation but does not say whether the landlord's consent is needed for the share sale. Check the lease for change-of-control provisions. If consent is required, make it a condition or a Seller deliverable.

### J. Supplier renewals (Disclosure §8)

Three Sandbar renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are described as "ordinary-course operating costs". The disclosure itself says it does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Their timing and split into three equal amounts also suggests they may have been structured to sit below thresholds or to avoid scrutiny. Read together, they look like pre-Completion commitments.

Push back:
- Obtain the contracts and check termination rights and total commitment.
- Treat unavoidable pre-Completion commitments outside the ordinary course as **debt-like** items, or as Seller costs.
- Warranty that no commitments outside the ordinary course have been entered into since the last accounts date.

### K. Mossvale (Disclosure §9)

DD-009 contains an assignment restriction, but the disclosure does not say whether consent is needed for a share sale. Get a legal view on whether a change of control triggers the restriction. If it does, obtain consent as a condition.

### L. Title (Disclosure §10; Clause on title)

The share register (DD-012) shows Harbourglass as holder of 100% of the shares, but the disclosure expressly says Wattlebridge has not done its own verification.

Push back:
- Wattlebridge should run its own **ASIC searches**, check the **statutory registers**, and obtain original share certificates and a transfer for all shares.
- PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares.
- Title and capacity warranties as **fundamental warranties** (section A above).
- Confirm stamp duty treatment and responsibility for it under NSW law.

### M. Tax and IP warranties (Seller update)

The Seller says tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime", which means they would be subject to the general cap, basket and 18-month period. Tax liabilities commonly emerge after 18 months, and IP ownership issues (particularly the Ironquay matter) are not general commercial risks.

Push back:
- Dedicated **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax, outside the basket and general cap, with the statute of limitations plus 60 days as the claims period.
- IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement, open-source, employee and contractor assignment) as fundamental or extended warranties.

---

## 3. Recommended structure

Known matters should not depend on general warranties. Because of the buyer-knowledge clause (even if removed, the Seller will resist), and because known issues are unlikely to be "claims" in the usual sense, these should be dealt with in the price and in **specific indemnities**:

1. **Price and funds flow:** deduct Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) and the debt-like items (bonuses, on-costs, unavoidable supplier commitments) from the price; reflect the Ironquay open fees.
2. **Conditions precedent:** Bluefen consent; Riverlark payout and discharge; Ironquay payment and confirmatory assignment; landlord and Mossvale consents if required; forensic report on DD-006.
3. **Specific indemnities:** Ironquay IP; privacy incident; pre-Completion tax; Bluefen-related losses if consent is waived; bonuses and on-costs; any undisclosed employee entitlements.
4. **Retention or escrow:** an amount sized to the open Ironquay fees, the privacy investigation, and a reasonable Bluefen contingency. (The amount should be set by the deal team.)
5. **Warranties:** the general package, but with the reset limitation terms in section 2A.
6. **Process:** updated data room index; bring-down; no general disclosure.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright:**
- The general data-room disclosure (§1.1–1.2) and the disclosure of "every fact" in the data room.
- Buyer-knowledge bar (Clause 8.3). Propose a pro-sandbagging clause.
- Treating title and capacity warranties as general warranties.
- Applying all limitations to all claims.
- "Release following Completion" for Riverlark.
- Treating Bluefen consent as satisfied on delivery, or on endeavours alone.
- Limiting Ironquay indemnity to the SOW3 payment.
- Excluding the bonuses from the funds flow.
- The "FINAL, not to be re-opened" position, which we have not accepted.

**Push back and renegotiate:**
- General cap: from 20% to a higher level, with title, tax and fraud at 100% or uncapped.
- Basket: move from deductible to tipping, lower the de minimis, and remove both for fundamental and specific claims.
- Time: from 18 months to 24–36 months for general warranties; tax to statute plus 60 days; fundamental warranties longer.
- Privacy and tax: specific indemnities outside the cap and basket.
- Supplier commitments and bonuses: debt-like treatment.

**Require before signing:**
- Bluefen written consent (or a CP with a long-stop and walk right).
- Riverlark payout letter and discharge in escrow.
- Ironquay payment evidence and confirmatory IP assignment.
- Forensic report on the DD-006 export incident, including whether notification is required.
- Contracts for Sandbar renewals and Mossvale and landlord consent position.
- Own title verification (ASIC, registers, PPSR, original share certificates).
- Refreshed data room index and bring-down to a date after 22 September 2026.

**Next steps for the deal team:**
1. Confirm whether the "principal-level" settlement the Seller refers to actually occurred. Nothing in our file shows it.
2. Set the negotiating range on the general cap and the time limits.
3. Instruct NSW counsel to review the sandbagging, limitation and stamp duty analysis.
4. Instruct tax advisers on the bonus on-costs, payroll tax and any tax indemnity scope.
5. Instruct privacy counsel on whether DD-006 is an eligible data breach.
6. Prepare the Wattlebridge mark-up and issues list for the Seller's counsel.

I can draft the issues list, the mark-up of Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12 and 13, or a short Seller-facing response letter once the deal team has confirmed the negotiating positions.

About AUD 180,000 is open per DD-010, and there is no evidence of payment or of a confirmatory assignment.

Push back:
- **Pre-signing:** obtain evidence of payment or a written confirmation from Ironquay, plus a confirmatory assignment of all Project Materials and IP.
- A **specific IP indemnity** covering title to all Ironquay-developed materials, not just the SOW3 fee, with recovery outside the basket and general cap.
- Retention of the open AUD 180k (or the full amount) from the price until title is confirmed.

### H. Privacy and export incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure §6)

The Seller characterises the DD-006 matter as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". The disclosure itself says the export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), that it was sent to an unintended external address, and that the investigation has not established whether anyone accessed it. This may be an **eligible data breach** under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme. If so, notification to the OAIC and affected individuals may be required, and regulatory exposure may follow.

Push back:
- Require a **forensic investigation** and written report before signing, including access logs, whether the link was opened or downloaded, and whether notification obligations have been assessed.
- A **specific indemnity** covering investigation, notification, remediation, regulatory penalties, complaints, and third-party claims, outside the basket, the general cap and the 18-month period.
- Warranties on privacy compliance and data security, with a longer survival period.
- Consider a separate escrow or retention for this matter.

### I. Office lease (Clause/Disclosure §7)

DD-007 identifies a notification obligation but does not say whether the landlord's consent is needed for the share sale. Check the lease for change-of-control provisions. If consent is required, make it a condition or a Seller deliverable.

### J. Supplier renewals (Disclosure §8)

Three Sandbar renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are described as "ordinary-course operating costs". The disclosure itself says it does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Their timing and split into three equal amounts also suggests they may have been structured to sit below thresholds or to avoid scrutiny. Read together, they look like pre-Completion commitments.

Push back:
- Obtain the contracts and check termination rights and total commitment.
- Treat unavoidable pre-Completion commitments outside the ordinary course as **debt-like** items, or as Seller costs.
- Warranty that no commitments outside the ordinary course have been entered into since the last accounts date.

### K. Mossvale (Disclosure §9)

DD-009 contains an assignment restriction, but the disclosure does not say whether consent is needed for a share sale. Get a legal view on whether a change of control triggers the restriction. If it does, obtain consent as a condition.

### L. Title (Disclosure §10; Clause on title)

The share register (DD-012) shows Harbourglass as holder of 100% of the shares, but the disclosure expressly says Wattlebridge has not done its own verification.

Push back:
- Wattlebridge should run its own **ASIC searches**, check the **statutory registers**, and obtain original share certificates and a transfer for all shares.
- PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares.
- Title and capacity warranties as **fundamental warranties** (section A above).
- Confirm stamp duty treatment and responsibility for it under NSW law.

### M. Tax and IP warranties (Seller update)

The Seller says tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime", which means they would be subject to the general cap, basket and 18-month period. Tax liabilities commonly emerge after 18 months, and IP ownership issues (particularly the Ironquay matter) are not general commercial risks.

Push back:
- Dedicated **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax, outside the basket and general cap, with the statute of limitations plus 60 days as the claims period.
- IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement, open-source, employee and contractor assignment) as fundamental or extended warranties.

## 3. Recommended structure

Known matters should not depend on general warranties. Because of the buyer-knowledge clause (even if removed, the Seller will resist), and because known issues are unlikely to be "claims" in the usual sense, these should be dealt with in the price and in **specific indemnities**:

1. **Price and funds flow:** deduct Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) and the debt-like items (bonuses, on-costs, unavoidable supplier commitments) from the price; reflect the Ironquay open fees.
2. **Conditions precedent:** Bluefen consent; Riverlark payout and discharge; Ironquay payment and confirmatory assignment; landlord and Mossvale consents if required; forensic report on DD-006.
3. **Specific indemnities:** Ironquay IP; privacy incident; pre-Completion tax; Bluefen-related losses if consent is waived; bonuses and on-costs; any undisclosed employee entitlements.
4. **Retention or escrow:** an amount sized to the open Ironquay fees, the privacy investigation, and a reasonable Bluefen contingency. (The amount should be set by the deal team.)
5. **Warranties:** the general package, but with the reset limitation terms in section 2A.
6. **Process:** updated data room index; bring-down; no general disclosure.
